response.sql: WITH player_totals AS (SELECT p.player_id, p.death_country, SUM(a.g_1b - a.g_cf) AS total FROM appearances a JOIN player p ON p.player_id = a.player_id WHERE a.g_1b IS NOT NULL AND a.g_cf IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.player_id, p.death_country), avg_total AS (SELECT AVG(total) AS avg_total FROM player_totals), above AS (SELECT pt.total, pt.total - at.avg_total AS excess FROM player_totals pt CROSS JOIN avg_total at WHERE pt.total > at.avg_total) SELECT SUM(total) AS sum_totals, AVG(excess) AS avg_excess FROM above;

assumptions.assumption: A player 'matches a player record' means an inner join on player_id, so appearances rows with no matching player row are dropped.

Rows are skipped individually when g_1b or g_cf is NULL, and a player's total is the sum of g_1b - g_cf over their remaining rows. A player with no valid rows has no total and is left out of the average.
'Average total' is the mean of per-player totals (one value per player), not a mean over appearance rows. Players are not weighted by how many rows they have.

Blank death_country is kept whether it is stored as NULL or as an empty string, because the query applies no filter on death_country. Each player has one player row, so grouping by death_country does not split players.
